### 2026-09-06 — Phase 1 step 4: anti-aliasing, scaling, accumulation

Audited §4.4/§4.5 first, as instructed. Third audit, third set of findings — this time none of
them wrong *numbers*, but two of them prescriptions that cannot be carried out: hardware
derivatives are undefined in a raymarcher's divergent loop, and `textureGrad()` needs a texture
this renderer deliberately does not have.

The instruction to make temporal stability a number before tuning it earned its keep in an
unexpected way. Establishing the baseline was straightforward; *verifying the guard* is what
exposed that the metric was unsound. A mutation that blanked the rim scored better than the
correct filter, because variance rewards an empty frame. The gate now has two halves and each is
verified by the mutation that trips it. That failure mode would have been invisible without
running the mutation — the metric looked perfectly reasonable.

The other two audit findings are now numbers rather than assertions: resolution scaling costs
2.14x the rim edge sharpness at 0.5x, and omitting the accumulation reset produces a ghosting
error of 134 of 255.

No appearance was tuned. Exposure and star brightness remain step 5 items. Still unregistered.
